correctness.rationale: For each fixed Lipschitz concave h with zero tips, arclength x density is 1/2+O_h(epsilon^2) uniformly a.e. Sorting three x-coordinates gives factor 6; only sign configurations with middle point on opposite branch have leading logarithmic mass. The middle-angle condition is uv<epsilon²(h(x-u)+h(x))(h(x+v)+h(x)), and in logarithmic bulk becomes uv<4epsilon²h(x)^2. Hyperbolic-area integration contributes 8h(x)^2 epsilon² log(1/epsilon); sign probability 1/4 and triple horizontal density 1/8 yield constant (3/2)Q. The change u=epsilon^t, v=4epsilon²h(x)²w/u and its Jacobian give conditional independent T Uniform(0,2), W Uniform(0,1), S fair and X density h²/Q in total variation after controlling endpoint strips. Jensen Q>B²/2 (strict due to zero tips) and Berwald Q<=2B²/3 (equality tents) yield 3B²/4<C<=B². Computed Q=16/15 and coefficient 8/5 for h=1-x²; Q=2/3, coefficient 1 for tent. Inspected finite Monte Carlo checker but did not rerun its 3-million-trial experiment; it does not prove the limit.
residual_risks: Total-variation proof requires controlling small x-tip and t-end strips using global product bound; source explicitly provides these arguments.
No uniform remainder across concave profiles or unbounded-slope ellipse cases.
